title: More AI leaders urge a slowdown, the White House says no - TCR 09/14/26
description:
OpenAI's Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis backed Anthropic's call to slow frontier AI while the White House called the alarm overblown, Y Combinator's Garry Tan urged US open-weight labs to distill frontier models openly, and two electric WeRide shuttles began passenger-free driverless testing at Zürich Airport with no driver or onboard safety monitor after 15,000 km of testing.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-september-14-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:42 Rival AI labs converge on a slowdown, the White House says no
3:48 Garry Tan's case for open distillation
6:52 Federal land opens as states write data-center rules
9:45 Zürich's driverless airport shuttle
12:20 The AI buildout orders forever chemicals
15:43 Close

This episode covers the rival labs converging on a slowdown and OpenAI adopting outside-evaluator access, the narrow safety-waiver and external-review-team proposal, Garry Tan's open-distillation argument, the Interior Department opening public land for data centers against Massachusetts Executive Order 658, Zürich Airport's driverless Level 4 shuttles, and a survey of ten of the world’s biggest PFAS makers that found nearly all plan to expand for AI.

On Saturday, September 12, the AI field's fiercest competitors converged. Sam Altman wrote that he agreed the industry needs to pace the frontier and said OpenAI would adopt the same permanent independent-evaluator access Anthropic pledged that day; Elon Musk answered "Dario is right," and DeepMind's Demis Hassabis called the direction correct. The proposed pause includes Anthropic’s intent to invite an independent external review team and asks Washington for a narrow antitrust waiver for certain safety conversations among frontier companies, so the safeguard that survives scrutiny is the one Anthropic committed to alone: outside verification. President Trump called the alarm overblown, while the administration moved to open federal public land for data centers, as Massachusetts barred permits for large campuses without local approval, sufficient incremental clean power or an alternative compliance payment, and general limits on permitting agencies' project NDAs. Y Combinator's Garry Tan urged US open-weight labs to distill frontier models openly and return capability trained on the commons back to the commons. Two electric WeRide shuttles began passenger-free test operation at Zürich Airport with no driver aboard, and a survey of ten of the world’s biggest PFAS makers found most expanding for AI cooling and chip fabrication even as lawsuits pushed two of them out.
